approach: Add one deterministic check, `check_reading_references`, to crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs and call it last from `check_reading_acceptance`. It scans the summary, assumptions and acceptance-criterion text for repo-path tokens (contain `/`, first segment a top-level directory of the snapshot or one of crates, docs, xtask, studies, .github). It refuses every token that is not a file or directory in `repo_files` (via the existing `path_exists_in`), not a create deliverable (or a directory above one), and not in a sentence that says the path is absent or to be created. With `repo_files` None, or a reading that declines or asks a question, it checks nothing. The error names each path and field and tells the reader to list the artifact as a create deliverable or say it does not exist. No model call. Tests sit beside the existing path-rule tests. CHANGELOG.md gets a Fixed entry and docs/decisions.md gets D147. Nothing keys on a job id. Round 2 change: criterion 5 now has a named seam and a fails_without, and the gate is shown by a regression test that the cargo gate runs.

decisions.choice: Put the check in reading acceptance as a new function called last from `check_reading_acceptance`, separate from `check_boundary_and_repo_files`.
decisions.reason: That is where an unverified reference is first accepted. A separate function leaves the boundary check's error and tests unchanged and lets the doc comment carry the root cause and the three job ids. The reader's one correction path (ReadError::Refused) already carries the message.

rejected.why: Its repair text and path_problems counting are tied to deliverables and banned words; mixing them complicates both.

rejected.option: Check job ids against landed state or queue position
rejected.why: Out of scope. Path presence in the snapshot is the observable fact later stages rely on.

rejected.option: Add a prose rule to the reader prompt
rejected.why: Prompt files are out of scope and prose is not enforced; the defaults ask for a mechanism.

decisions.choice: Check only path-shaped tokens that contain `/` and start at a known top-level directory. Skip tokens with wildcard, placeholder or URL characters, absolute paths, and slash-less names such as `reading.rs`.
decisions.reason: A bare basename is usually shorthand for a file elsewhere in the tree; checking it would refuse ordinary readings. Every full repo path is still covered, so the class is covered.

rejected.option: Check bare root file names such as foo.md
rejected.why: Abbreviations and examples would cause false refusals; the refusal rate must stay near the expected 3%.

rejected.option: Match any word containing a dot
rejected.why: It matches `e.g.`, version numbers and identifiers.

decisions.choice: Exempt a path that is a create deliverable, a directory above a create deliverable, or sits in a sentence with an absence or creation phrase (const list: `not exist`, `absent`, `missing`, `no such`, `not yet`, `be created`, `new file`, `creates`). Exempt `CHANGELOG.md`. Sentences split at `. `, newline or `;`.
decisions.reason: These are the two repairs the brief allows, and the check must accept them. Sentence splitting stops one absence statement from exempting a different path elsewhere.

rejected.why: The brief requires accepting text that states the path does not exist.

rejected.option: Exempt modify and delete deliverables as well
rejected.why: Those already exist and are checked by the existing deliverable rule.

decisions.choice: Scan summary, assumptions[i] and acceptance_criteria[i].text only; skip a reading with no capability or with a question.
decisions.reason: This is the scope the brief names, and the existing path rule skips the same cases. out_of_scope text names things not touched and would add noise.

rejected.option: Scan every text field including out_of_scope and departures
rejected.why: More false refusals for little gain.

decisions.choice: Show criterion 5 by the real cargo gate commands, run as separate simple commands, with the new tests as the content that makes the gate meaningful: test seam is `cargo test --locked` running the whole workspace, which includes the athena-core tests that call `check_reading_acceptance`.
decisions.reason: The criterion is that the gate passes with the change; it fails if the change breaks an existing test (for example a reading text in an existing test now naming an absent path) or if the new tests fail.

rejected.why: The verifier may run only whole simple commands, so each is listed separately.

files.purpose: Add `check_reading_references` with a doc comment (root cause, the three job ids), a path-token scanner and absence-phrase const; call it last from `check_reading_acceptance` and update that doc comment; add unit tests.
Add a Fixed entry under Unreleased: root cause, the check, and the repair the refusal asks for.
Add D147 after D146: case, root cause, decision, rejected alternatives, tradeoff, reversal cost, provenance.

steps: Read reading.rs around `path_exists_in` (line ~2742), `check_boundary_and_repo_files` (~2771), `check_reading_acceptance` (~2849) and the tests near `governed_reading` (~6349) and `files_at_head`/`reading_with_deliverable` (~6640) to reuse them.

Add private helpers near `path_exists_in`: `path_tokens(text) -> Vec<String>` (maximal run of [A-Za-z0-9_./-]; skip a token whose neighbour is one of `*<>{}$` or is part of `://`, a token that starts with `/`, `.` or `~`, has `..` or an empty segment, or has no `/`; trim trailing `.` and `/`), `sentence_of(text, token)` (split at `. `, newline or `;`), and a const `ABSENCE_PHRASES`.

Add `pub fn check_reading_references(reading, repo_files) -> Result<()>`. Return Ok when repo_files is None, capability is None or a question is set. Derive top-level directories from `repo_files`, plus crates, docs, xtask, studies and .github. For summary, assumptions[i] and acceptance_criteria[i], find each token that is not in the snapshot (`path_exists_in`), not a Create deliverable (or a directory above one), not CHANGELOG.md, and not in a sentence with an absence phrase. Collect each path with its field label once and bail with a message naming them, saying the snapshot lacks them, and giving the repair: list it as a create deliverable, or say it does not exist. Doc comment names the root cause (reading acceptance never compared the reading's references with the snapshot) and jobs 20261026-042558-5p65, 20261026-064950-38jx and 20261026-065228-02zf.
Call it last in `check_reading_acceptance` (`check_boundary_and_repo_files(...)?; check_reading_references(reading, repo_files)`) and extend that function's doc comment.

Add tests: absent-path refusal in summary, assumption and criterion naming path and field (`a_reading_that_relies_on_an_absent_path_is_refused_and_the_path_is_named`); acceptance cases a to g (`the_reference_rule_accepts_*`); repair text (`the_reference_refusal_tells_the_reader_how_to_repair_it`); a `files_with_core()` helper.
Add the CHANGELOG.md Fixed entry under `## [Unreleased]` (naming `check_reading_references`, root cause, the repair) and D147 in docs/decisions.md after D146.
Run `cargo fmt --all`, then `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --locked`, and fix findings.

risks.risk: False refusals of good readings: criteria often mention test or output paths the producer creates but does not list as deliverables.
risks.mitigation: The refusal names the path and says to list it as a create deliverable or state that it does not exist, so the reader repairs it in its one correction. Globs, placeholders, URLs, absolute paths and slash-less names are skipped, and tests cover each.

risks.risk: The tokenizer takes in trailing punctuation or `path:line` suffixes and refuses a real file.
risks.mitigation: Maximal run of [A-Za-z0-9_./-], trailing `.` and `/` trimmed, `:` ends the token. Tests cover trailing dot, backticks, parentheses and `reading.rs:2849`.

risks.risk: An existing test with `Some(&files)` breaks because its reading text holds a path absent from the small files_at_head set.
risks.mitigation: The producer greps the tests module for text fields near `Some(&files)` and runs the athena-core tests; the first segment must be a known top-level directory, and the texts seen were generic.

risks.risk: The production call site (`read_for`, ~line 637) now refuses text the old rule accepted, and a refusal loop wastes reader spend.
risks.mitigation: The refusal reuses the existing one-correction path, so no new loop is added; the message is specific.

risks.risk: Directory handling: `crates/athena-core/src` must pass, and a name that only shares a prefix must not.
risks.mitigation: Use the existing `path_exists_in`, which tests the prefix with a trailing `/`; a test covers both.

demonstrations.method: Unit test in reading.rs. It builds a reading with the existing `governed_reading` helper (a modify of crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs, so the deliverable rule passes) and sets the assumption to a sentence saying crates/athena-core/src/design_review.rs already exists. It calls `check_reading_acceptance(&reading, "add a greeting", None, &[], Some(&files))` where `files` is a BTreeSet holding crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs but not design_review.rs. The same sentence is also put in the summary and in an acceptance criterion.
demonstrations.observes: The call returns Err; the message contains crates/athena-core/src/design_review.rs and the label `assumptions[0]` (and `summary`, `acceptance_criteria[0]` in the other cases).
demonstrations.fails_without: Without check_reading_references, check_reading_acceptance returns Ok for the reading, so the unwrap_err in the test panics and the test fails.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry point `check_reading_acceptance` (exists, line ~2849). Fixture `governed_reading` (exists, line ~6349) and a local BTreeSet of paths passed as the `repo_files` argument (the argument exists). A small `files_with_core()` helper is added to the tests module in step 5. No double replaces any logic.

demonstrations.method: Unit tests in reading.rs on the same reading as criterion 1: (a) accepted when `files` holds the path; (b) accepted when the path is also a Create deliverable; (c) accepted when the sentence says the path does not exist or is to be created, while a second still-absent path in a different sentence is refused; (d) accepted with repo_files None; (e) a table of different absent paths (docs/design/other.md, xtask/src/new.rs, .github/workflows/x.yml, studies/a/b.md) each refused; (f) glob, URL, bare `reading.rs`, trailing-dot and `path:123` forms handled as stated; (g) a reading with a question or no capability accepted.
demonstrations.observes: Ok in cases a, b, c (first path), d, f and g; Err naming the path in case e and the second path in case c. No job id appears in any assertion.
demonstrations.fails_without: An over-broad check would refuse the accepted cases. A check keyed on one job id or one path would not refuse the different paths in the table, so case e fails; with the check removed, case e and the second path of case c fail.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry point `check_reading_acceptance` with `repo_files` as `Some(&files)` or `None` (exists). Inputs from `governed_reading` (exists) and `reading_with_deliverable` (exists, line ~6648). No fake.

demonstrations.method: Grep reading.rs for the new function name and the three job ids, then read the lines to see the call inside `check_reading_acceptance` and the doc comment.
demonstrations.observes: A definition of `check_reading_references`, a call to it in the body of `check_reading_acceptance` after `check_boundary_and_repo_files`, and a doc comment naming the root cause (reading acceptance never compared the reading's references with the snapshot) and the three job ids.

demonstrations.method: Unit test asserts the refusal text contains the path, advice to list it as a create deliverable, and advice to say it does not exist. Then grep CHANGELOG.md for the new entry.
demonstrations.observes: The error tells the reader to list the artifact as a create deliverable or say it does not exist. `grep -n "check_reading_references" CHANGELOG.md` finds the entry under `## [Unreleased]`.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the message lacks the repair text, the assertions on `create deliverable` and `does not exist` fail.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry point `check_reading_acceptance` (exists); same fixtures as criterion 1; the message text is produced by the production check, not the test.

demonstrations.method: Run the three gate commands, each as its own simple command, on the finished tree. The test run includes every existing athena-core test that calls `check_reading_acceptance` or `read_for` with `Some(&files)`, so a reading text that now names an absent repo path is caught, as are the new tests.
demonstrations.observes: Exit 0 for `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --locked`, with the new tests listed as passing. The function reads no model and no clock, so results are deterministic.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the change were missing or wrong, the new tests from criteria 1, 2 and 4 would fail under `cargo test --locked`; if it breaks an existing test fixture (a text naming an absent path), that test fails; formatting or lint errors in the new code fail the fmt and clippy runs.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry points: the workspace test harness running `check_reading_acceptance` through the athena-core unit tests (exists), plus `cargo fmt` and `cargo clippy` over the tree. Fixtures are the existing test helpers `governed_reading`, `files_at_head` and `reading_with_deliverable` (exist); the new tests are added by step 5. No fake.

open_questions: Bare root file names (for example Cargo.lock) and slash-less basenames are not checked, because they are often shorthand. Say so if the user wants root files checked; the check could then require that no file in the snapshot has that basename.
The brief expects about 3% of readings to be newly refused. The code does not settle the real rate; no replay fixture of stored readings with a file set was found.
The absence-phrase list is a judgment. A reader who words it differently is refused once; the refusal text says how to repair it.
